mission: Verify-pass per operator's 'don't trust verify' directive. Re-grounded in CLAUDE.md + CLAUDE_ROOT.md. Re-ran all four root gates plus tapit-attest tests fresh, all green. Adversarial code review of Phase 2.5 surface found one real bug: three call sites compute entry-digest as sha256(JSON.stringify(attestation)) instead of the canonical envelopeId(att) exported by tapit-attest. That breaks (1) determinism across engines, (2) OTS commit semantics, (3) URL stability across added signatures (Phase 2.6 witnesses would break every existing entry's URL), AND it duplicates a library responsibility. Fixing across createJournalEntry, JournalCard, JournalDetail. Other findings flagged in the close-out report, not fixed in this pass.

mission: Anchor-worker polish — fetch timeout via wrapped OtsTransport with AbortController (30s timeout per request), plus exponential backoff in the worker's processOne so failed rows skip until next-attempt-time arrives (min(5min × 2^attempts, 1hr)). Multi-tab coordination deferred — most users hit one tab; the cost of two tabs both stamping is wasted network + the queue dedupes by digest anyway.

reason: Wrapped the OpenTimestampsProvider with a custom transport that uses AbortController + 30s timeout per request. tapit-attest's OtsProvider accepts transport injection so no library change. TS BodyInit narrowing required a 'as BodyInit | undefined' cast on init.body (Uint8Array accepted at runtime).

Exponential backoff: failed rows are skipped in processOne until their last_attempt + min(5min × 2^(attempts-1), 1hr) has elapsed. Queued and pending rows still process on every scan — only 'failed' state backs off. Doctrine comment in the file header updated.

mission: Phase 3 — Layer 2 inter-app deeplink pathway per DESIGN.md/PLAN.md. Third-party apps construct a deeplink with a base64-encoded SignRequest; the wallet decodes it, renders a plain-English approval screen showing origin + callback-host + what's being signed, signs on approve and redirects to the callback URL with a SignGrant, redirects with a structured SignDecline on user-declined or invalid-request. Composes from tapit-attest primitives — wallet.attest builds via the right builder per kind, wallet.sign appends the signature, envelopeId is the stable id for the anchor queue. Keys-never-leave preserved (signing local, only public envelopes in the grant). The approval screen is the product per DESIGN.md §9 — never a JSON dump.

Library work: replace tapit-attest/src/core/field-tree.ts's stub disclosureProof with a real implementation that produces a proof bundle (envelope-meta + disclosed leaf + sibling-hashes per level up to root + signatures), and add verifyDisclosureProof that recomputes the claim root from the leaf+siblings, recomputes the canonical attestation digest from envelope-meta + claim-root, and verifies signatures using the existing quorum-of-good rule. reason: Exported metaHash so the selective-disclosure verifier in field-tree.ts can recompute the canonical attestation digest from meta-fields + recovered claim root without duplicating envelope.ts's hashing logic. Same bytes the signer used.

Replaced the stub disclosureProof with a real implementation that walks the path and records sibling hashes at each branch level. Added verifyDisclosureProof that recomputes the claim root from leaf+siblings, recomputes attestationDigest via metaHash + tagged hash, runs quorum-of-good signature verification. DisclosureProofBundle shape: meta (envelope fields needed to recompute metaHash) + leaf + steps (root-down sibling-hash path) + signatures.

Replaced the v1.1-throws stub test with five real round-trip tests: signed-attestation proof verifies, only the disclosed leaf appears in the serialized proof (siblings are hashes), tampered leaf value fails verification, tampered meta-field fails verification, path errors (missing segment, branch-not-leaf) throw with friendly messages.

mission: Add netlify.toml at repo root so Netlify auto-detects build settings rather than requiring dashboard config. Build command + publish dir + Node 20. SPA fallback so client-side routes (/entry/:digest, /verify, /sign, /settings, /auth/callback) survive refresh. Basic security headers. No CSP because it's a footgun for a wallet that talks to Supabase + OTS calendar; operator can add later if wanted.

mission: Operator reported photo capture not working post-deploy. Fix: drop capture=environment attribute from the photo input (suspected iOS PWA standalone interaction where camera returns but file input doesn't pick up the result), add HEIC→JPEG normalization in the composer so iPhone photos render on non-Safari devices (cross-device portability footgun closed), and surface any photo-save error more visibly. Smallest useful fix; ship, ask operator to retry, then move to Supabase Storage for media in Cut 2.

reason: Helper that re-encodes any non-renderable image format (HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, etc.) to JPEG at 0.92 quality via a canvas. iPhone captures in HEIC by default; HEIC renders in Safari but not Chrome-on-Android or most desktop viewers. The re-encode runs once at composer pick-time so storage and the detail-view tag both work with a portable JPEG.

Dropped capture=environment from the photo input (suspected iOS PWA standalone issue where the camera returned but the file input did not pick up the result). iOS now shows the standard file-picker sheet which still offers Take Photo plus Photo Library plus Choose File — one extra tap than direct camera but reliable across Safari tab and installed-PWA modes. New onPickAttachment handler runs normalizeImage on every picked file, with visible 'Reading photo…' state during the async re-encode and visible '✓ filename (type)' confirmation when ready. Errors from normalize surface as the existing error banner.
Listed normalizeImage.ts in touches.
